literal: Without going, if the owner remains, the land, feeling neglected, like a wife, will feign anger.
translation: If the owner remains idle without visiting his field, the land, feeling neglected, will sulk and feign anger like a wife.
modern: நிலத்தின் உரிமையாளன் நிலத்திற்குச் செல்லாமல் சோம்பேறியாக இருந்தால், அவனது நிலமானது தன்னை அவன் கைவிட்டுவிட்டதாக எண்ணி, அவனது மனைவி ஊடல் கொள்வது போலக் கோபித்துக் கொள்ளும்.
explanation: This couplet uses a beautiful domestic metaphor to emphasize the necessity of constant personal attention in agriculture. The poet compares the land to a wife (illāḷ) who expects her husband's presence and care. If the owner (kiḻavaṉ) remains idle and fails to visit his fields (cellāṉ iruppiṉ), the land feels neglected (pulantu) and reacts with resentment (ūṭi viṭum), refusing to yield its bounty. Just as a neglected wife withdraws her affection, the neglected earth withdraws her fertility, showing that farming requires daily devotion and cannot be managed from afar.
